threads.body: [Style] Classes under `javaagent/src/main` are internal implementation details and should not be declared `final` (`docs/contributing/style-guide.md:101-104`). Remove `final` here.

Quoted `ObjectName` property values are returned with their JMX quotes and escapes intact. For a valid pool name containing a comma or another special character, this therefore emits the serialized JMX value rather than the actual pool name; unquote quoted values before using them as metric attributes.

`ApacheDbcpSingletons.getDataSourceName(ObjectName)` is the same code but does not unquote, so an identically configured pool reports a name that still carries the `ObjectName` quotes and backslash escapes. That encoding is transport syntax, not part of the pool identity, and quoted values are common (any name containing `,`, `:`, `=`, or a quote). Since the two modules are clones, can we align them here? Preferably by hoisting this into `JdbcConnectionPoolNameUtil` as an `ObjectName` overload, since both modules already depend on `jdbc:library` and that leaves a single implementation; otherwise by copying the unquoting and its test into `apache-dbcp-2.0`.

replies.body:
I aligned Tomcat DBCP with the existing Apache DBCP behavior by removing the Tomcat-specific ObjectName unquoting. Both modules now use getKeyProperty("name") as-is and fall back to ObjectName.toString() when the property is absent.

This intentionally preserves the ObjectName-encoded representation. Shared normalization for both modules can be considered separately if we decide that the pool identity should use the decoded value.
